newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Chronology - Italy bids to join the ERM grid.
newsitem.headline: Chronology - Italy bids to join the ERM grid.

text.p: European Union finance ministers and central bankers were to meet on Sunday to seek a compromise over the Italian lira's return to the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM).

On Saturday, the EU monetary committee failed to agree on terms of the lira's re-entry after four years of absence from the system, which is designed to provide monetary stability to member countries.

If lira joins it will likely be allowed to fluctuate within a 15 percent band against other currencies, the same terms as apply to the present 11 members, except the German mark and Dutch guilder, which move within a narrow 2.25 percent range.

Italy is bidding to return to the ERM at a time when the grid has successfully provided relative stability to its members for the last three years, following earlier turmoils that saw the lira as well as the British pound crash out.
The following is a chronology of events since 1992:
-- June 2, 1992 - Danes vote no to the Maastricht treaty. Markets start to question plans for a single currency.
-- June 3 - In a political gamble, French President Francois Mitterrand announces France will hold a referendum on Maastricht in the autumn. Markets are plunged into period of uncertainty.
-- July 16 - German Bundesbank announces shock 0.75 percentage point rise in its discount rate to a record 8.75 percent. The mark begins a relentless rise against other European currencies.
-- Sept 5 - Finance ministers, meeting under pressure in Bath, England, stress they have no plans for ERM realignment.
-- Sept 8 - Turmoil on European markets sweeps north as Finland severs the markka's link to the European Currency Unit and allows a devaluation. Sweden and Italy raise interest rates.
-- Sept 10 - British Prime Minister John Major rules out devaluation within ERM as "a betrayal of our future".
-- Sept 13 - First major realignment of the ERM since January 1987 as behind-the-scenes deal brings seven percent devaluation of the lira in return for a cut in German interest rates.
-- Sept 14 - Bundesbank announces quarter point cut in Lombard rate and half point cut in discount rate. Markets say too little too late and pressure on pound and lira resumes.

-- Sept 16 - "Black Wednesday." Markets attack pound, lira and peseta, forcing them below ERM floors. Central banks intervene and Britain announces unprecedented two-stage rise in base rate from 10 to 15 percent, then suspends pound from ERM and reduces rate to 12 percent. Swedish overnight rate to 500 percent.
-- Sept 17 - After a six-hour meeting, EU's monetary committee suspends lira from ERM. Peseta devalued by five percent and Britain cuts reduces base rate to 10 percent.
-- Sept 20 - French voters narrowly approve Maastricht treaty, but result doesn't prevent more attacks on weak ERM currencies.
-- Sept 23 - France and Germany launch counter-offensive against currency speculation that threatens to blow ERM apart. They appear to hold the line and markets calm down.
-- Nov 19 - Period of calm ends. Sweden abandons efforts to peg crown to the European currency unit, sparking new turmoil.
-- Nov 22 - Portugal and Spain devalue by six percent. Markets attack Irish punt, Danish crown and French franc but ERM intact.
-- Dec 12 - EU summit in Edinburgh reaffirms commitment to Maastricht treaty, saying ratification is needed for EU to remain anchor of stability in fast-changing continent.
-- Jan 7, 1993 - Ireland raises overnight interest rates from 50 to 100 percent to fight off renewed speculation against the punt.
-- Jan 30 - After more speculation Ireland devalues punt by 10 percent -- biggest single devaluation in 14 years of ERM.
-- Feb 1 - Market attention switches to Danish crown, but central bank intervention deflects it.
-- April 19 - Finance ministers unveil 35 billion European currency unit ($42 billion) plan to boost faltering Community economies and create jobs. Plan fails to impress money markets.
-- May 13 - After two weeks of speculative pressure, peseta devalued by eight percent and escudo by 6.5 percent.
-- May 18 - Danes vote in favour of Maastricht treaty at second referendum but vote fails to quash speculation that the move to monetary union is off the rails.
-- June 21/22 - EU summit in Copenhagen launches major review of labour market and strategies for growth, and calls for quick cuts in European interest rates.
-- July 1 - After pressure at end of June, Bundesbank pursues policy of gradual rate cuts but markets unimpressed.

-- July 29 - Bundesbank snubs market speculation that it will cut up to half a percentage point off the key discount rate to save the ERM, chosing to leave the rate untouched and shaving half a point of the less important Lombard. Weak ERM currencies come under tremendous pressure in foreign exchange markets.
-- July 30 - Selling continues, pushing French franc through ERM floor several times. Central banks intervene.
-- July 31 - Monetary Committee meets to consider what can be done to hold the system together.

-- Aug 1 - The Committee hands its proposals to an emergency session of EU finance ministers and central bank governors. After 12 hours of talks, early in the morning of Aug 2 they announce a major reshaping of the ERM, allowing all its currencies except the German mark and Dutch guilder to fluctuate by 15 percent above and below their central rates. The mark and guilder maintain a 2.25 percent range.

-- Jan 8, 1995 - Austrian schilling joins the ERM with 15 percent fluctuation bands at a central rate of 13.7167 schillings per Ecu and 14.2136 marks per 100 schillings. Before entry the shilling had for 15 years closely shadowed the mark, hovering within a narrow 0.25 pecent margin.

-- Oct 14, 1996 - Finland joins the ERM with 15 percent fluctution bands at a central rate of 5.80661 markka per ecu and 3.04 markka to the mark. The move undelines Helsinki's comittment to a joint currency in Europe and puts pressure on Italy to join in its wake.
-- Nov 23 - Monetary committee fails to agree central rate for lira to re-enter ERM.
-- Nov 24 - EU finance ministers and central bank heads meet in Brussels to determine the rate at which lira could re-enter the ERM.
